questions.question: On a Brazil instance, a security administrator plans to use the Basic Auth Restriction page to limit Basic Authentication without unexpectedly blocking working integrations. Which approach do the release notes recommend?

options.text: Run the tracking period to find Basic Auth users, then enable enforcement
Enable enforcement first, then build the allowlist from the blocked requests
Grant the admin role to each integration user, then enable enforcement
Turn off the feature toggle, then switch on the enforcement toggle

explanation.correct: Brazil adds the Basic Auth Restriction page, which limits Basic Authentication access to a defined allowlist. The release notes say to run the tracking period first to identify users currently relying on Basic Auth, and only then enable enforcement to block Basic Auth requests that don't match the allowlist. In tracking mode, accounts using basic authentication are recorded but no requests are blocked. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-authentication-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the documented order. Enforcement blocks Basic Auth requests that don't match the allowlist, so enabling it first would block legitimate integrations. The release notes say to run the tracking period first and then enable enforcement.

The admin role is not one of the documented ways to pass enforcement. Once enforcement is enabled, requests are blocked unless the account has Web Services Access Only (WSAO), presents a valid MFA one-time password, or has the snc_basic_auth_api_access role.

Turning off the feature toggle disables the feature completely: when it is unchecked, no enforcement occurs, and the enforcement toggle has no effect. This does not identify which accounts rely on Basic Auth.

source.excerpt: Run the tracking period first to identify users currently relying on Basic Auth, then enable enforcement to block Basic Auth requests that don't match the allowlist.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, an administrator wants to know what the release adds to warn the team before a SAML SP signing keystore expires and single sign-on starts failing. What does the instance now do?

options.text: It shows home page banners that link to a Security Center customer action
It emails one expiry notice to every user who has the admin role
It renews the expiring keystore by itself and records that in the system log
It suspends SAML single sign-on until the keystore is replaced

explanation.correct: Brazil adds SAML certificate expiry notifications: when SP signing or encryption keystores are nearing or past expiry, administrators get banner alerts on the home page. Separate banners appear for signing and for encryption certificates, and each one links to a dedicated customer action in Security Center so the admin can act before SSO is disrupted. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-authentication-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The new Brazil alerting is home page banner alerts (one for signing, one for encryption certificates). The release notes only say the existing SAML certificate expiry notification now triggers earlier with more keystore detail; they do not describe a single notice emailed to every admin user.
The feature only alerts administrators so they can manage certificates proactively; the release notes do not describe the instance renewing keystores on its own.
The notifications exist so administrators can act before SSO is disrupted and to reduce authentication failures; nothing in the release notes says SSO is suspended.

source.excerpt: The instance displays two separate banners — one for signing certificates and one for encryption certificates — each linking to a dedicated customer action in Security Center.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, a release manager must be able to request, cancel, and schedule clones in Clone Admin Console. Which role must be granted, and on which instance?

options.text: clone_admin on the source instance
oauth_admin on the source instance
soap on the target instance
security_admin on the source instance

explanation.correct: The Brazil additional requirements for Clone Admin Console state that the clone_admin role is required to request, cancel, or schedule clones. The OAuth clone docs also say the clone_admin role is required on the source instance to request clones. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The oauth_admin role is needed only on the target instance during the initial OAuth setup. It is not required on the source instance and is not the role for requesting, canceling, or scheduling clones.
The security_admin role is the one required to make changes on the Basic Auth Restriction page. Clone Admin Console requires clone_admin to request, cancel, or schedule clones.

The soap role is only needed on the target-instance user when cloning falls back to Basic Auth, together with clone_admin and identity_type set to machine. It does not let anyone request or schedule clones.

source.excerpt: The clone_admin role is required to request, cancel, or schedule clones.

questions.question: After upgrading from Zurich to Brazil, an administrator registers a target instance for OAuth 2.0 clone authentication in Clone Admin Console. When is the oauth_admin role required on that target instance?

options.text: During the one-time OAuth setup of that target
Each time a clone request is sent to that target
Each time a scheduled clone is canceled or changed
Whenever a clone falls back to Basic Auth

explanation.correct: The release notes state that the oauth_admin role is required on the target instance during initial OAuth setup only. Registration happens once per target: after setup, the source instance automatically gets a short-lived JWT access token before each clone request, so no admin credentials are entered per request. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: After setup, Instance Clone uses a short-lived JWT access token that the source instance obtains automatically before each clone operation. OAuth setup is required once per target instance, and routine clone requests need no re-registration.
Requesting, canceling, or scheduling clones requires the clone_admin role. The oauth_admin role is required on the target only during the initial OAuth setup.
The Basic Auth fallback requires the target-instance user to have the clone_admin role, the soap role, and identity_type set to machine. The oauth_admin role is not part of that list.

source.excerpt: The oauth_admin role is required on the target instance during initial OAuth setup only.

questions.question: After upgrading from Zurich to Brazil, an administrator reviews the Clone Admin Console release notes. According to the notes, what was the Clone Home menu item renamed to?

options.text: Clone Activity
Clone Summary
Instance Overview
Configuration

explanation.correct: The Clone Admin Console release notes (listed for both Australia and Brazil) state that the Clone Home menu item has been renamed to Clone Activity to be more descriptive of the page's purpose and improve navigation clarity. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-cloneadminconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Clone summary is a separate feature that highlights clones scheduled in the next 30 days that involve the same target instance. It is not the new name of the Clone Home menu item.
Instance Overview is the tab that now shows last-cloned timestamps for each instance. The renamed menu item is Clone Activity.
The Configuration tab groups all clone-related settings in one place. The release notes say Clone Home was renamed to Clone Activity, not merged into Configuration.

source.excerpt: The Clone Home menu item has been renamed to Clone Activity to be more descriptive of the page's purpose and improve navigation clarity.

questions.question: A data steward on an Australia instance needs to perform basic Data Management tasks without being given the full admin role. Which granular admin role did the Australia release introduce for this?

options.text: The data_mgmt_tools_admin role
The delegated_developer role
The events_admin role
The context_rollback_executor role

explanation.correct: The Data Management release notes list a granular admin role under Australia: administrators can perform basic Data Management tasks when granted the data_mgmt_tools_admin role instead of the full admin role. The roles page describes it as a granular admin role that reduces the need to grant full admin access. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-datamanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: delegated_developer is one of the extra roles that must be assigned alongside data_mgmt_tools_admin (for access to tables, columns, and application scopes). It is not the granular Data Management admin role.
events_admin must also be assigned alongside data_mgmt_tools_admin so the user can write trigger data for scheduling jobs. It is not the granular admin role introduced for Data Management.
context_rollback_executor is an additional role needed alongside data_mgmt_tools_admin to roll back updated or deleted records. It is not the granular Data Management admin role.

source.excerpt: Enable administrators to perform basic Data Management tasks by granting the data_mgmt_tools_admin role instead of the full admin role.

questions.question: After upgrading to Australia, a developer looks at the new Read Only Option on a sys_dictionary record to lock down a field. Which two statements about the options are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Strict Read Only blocks changes in the UI and by g_form.setValue()
Display Read Only looks read-only but still allows updates by API
Display Read Only also blocks updates made through any API
The existing read_only field stays editable on the dictionary form
Strict Read Only still lets users change the field on the form

explanation.correct: The Table Builder release notes (Australia) state that a new Read Only Option was added to sys_dictionary and sys_dictionary_override. With Display Read Only, the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs. With Strict Read Only, the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as g_form.setValue(). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-tablebuilder-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the opposite: with Display Read Only the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs.
The release notes state that the existing read_only field is now locked and cannot be edited in the UI. Field behavior depends on the selected Read Only Option.
With Strict Read Only, the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as g_form.setValue(), so users cannot change it on the form.

source.excerpt: With Display Read Only , the field appears read-only but can still be updated through APIs. With Strict Read Only , the field can't be changed in the UI or by client scripts such as [ g_form.setValue() ].

questions.question: During an Australia upgrade of a non-production instance, several ATF tests fail. Where in Upgrade Console can the administrator open the ATF troubleshooting agent?

options.text: The Conduct post-testing step of post-upgrade activities
The Choose an upgrade plan step of pre-upgrade activities
The Store application upgrades step of post-upgrade
The Bulk application update console for the upgrade

explanation.correct: The Upgrade Console release notes list ATF Troubleshooting agent access under Australia: you can troubleshoot failed tests by accessing the ATF troubleshooting agent from the Conduct post-testing step in the post-upgrade activities of a non-production instance. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-upgradeconsole-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Choose an upgrade plan step (added in Zurich) is where you select or create an upgrade plan before upgrading. It is not where the ATF troubleshooting agent is accessed.
The Store application upgrades step shows App updates and Upgrade store applications information and offers the Sync Now option. The ATF troubleshooting agent is in the Conduct post-testing step.
The Bulk application update console (Australia) is for reviewing, selecting, and updating multiple applications at once. It does not provide the ATF troubleshooting agent.

source.excerpt: You can now troubleshoot failed tests by accessing the ATF troubleshooting agent from the Conduct post-testing step in the post-upgrade activities of a non-production instance.

questions.question: On an Australia instance, an administrator wants to add a UI interaction to a Configurable Workspace page by applying it through a declarative action. What does the release note say this approach allows?

options.text: Extending the page without taking ownership of it
Changing the base action itself to override attributes
Triggering it from declarative actions but not page events
Applying it after first taking ownership of the page

explanation.correct: The Configurable Workspace release notes (Australia) state that a UI interaction combines logic, script, and configurable UI and can be applied from any page event or declarative action. When you use a declarative action to apply a UI interaction, you can extend a page without taking ownership. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurableworkspace-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Australia notes say you can override attributes without altering the base action, so the base action does not need to be changed.
A UI interaction can be applied from any page event or declarative action, so page events are supported too.
This is the opposite of the documented benefit: applying a UI interaction with a declarative action lets you extend a page without taking ownership.

source.excerpt: When you use a declarative action to apply a UI interaction, you can extend a page without taking ownership.

questions.question: An Employee Center administrator must make the title of the Topic Header widget fit the organization's heading structure so screen reader and keyboard users can navigate pages clearly. Which capability supports this?

options.text: Setting the widget's heading level, H1 to H6, in its instance options
Turning on automatic translation of widgets into the browser language
Applying a high-contrast theme to every portal page for all users
Hiding the widget title so that screen readers skip over the heading

explanation.correct: The Australia and Brazil releases let administrators configure widget heading levels (H1 to H6) to meet organizational standards and support assistive technologies. In Employee Center the admin opens the widget's instance options (for example on the Topic Header widget) and picks the title heading level, giving pages a clear heading hierarchy for screen reader and keyboard users. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-employeecenter-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Employee Center accessibility enhancement in the release notes is configurable widget heading levels; it does not translate widgets, and translation would not fix the heading structure.
A site-wide high-contrast theme is not the capability described; the release notes describe per-widget heading levels from H1 to H6 to build a clear heading hierarchy.
Removing the heading works against the goal: the docs say clear heading hierarchies are what improve navigation for screen reader and keyboard users.

source.excerpt: Improve accessibility by allowing admins to configure widget heading levels (H1–H6) to meet organizational standards and support technologies.

questions.question: An administrator setting up a new Brazil instance wants unregistered users to request accounts and looks for the User Registration Request plugin (com.snc.user_registration). What should the administrator expect?

options.text: It is hidden and not activated on new instances, yet still supported
It is removed from every instance as part of the Brazil upgrade
It is activated by default so the welcome screen shows the request form
It is replaced by a Store app that must be installed before upgrading

explanation.correct: Starting with Brazil, the User Registration Request plugin is being prepared for future deprecation. It is hidden and no longer activated on new instances, but it continues to be supported. The user self-registration docs add that the External User Self-Registration plugin provides the latest experience for this functionality. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-identity-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The plugin is only being prepared for future deprecation; the docs state it will continue to be supported, so it is not removed during the upgrade.
The opposite is true: from Brazil the plugin is hidden and no longer activated on new instances, so the request form is not there by default.
The docs point to the External User Self-Registration plugin for the latest experience, but the old plugin stays supported and nothing must be installed before upgrading.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Brazil release, User Registration Request plugin (com.snc.user_registration) is being prepared for future deprecation. It will be hidden and no longer activated on new instances but will continue to be supported.

questions.question: After the Brazil upgrade, a service desk lead tries to set the Conditional Script Writer group as the assignment group on an incident and cannot select it. What explains this?

options.text: The group is permission-only and is blocked as an assignment group
The upgrade deleted the group and replaced it with a single role
The group now accepts only members who hold the admin role
Auto-assignment must be turned off before the group can be selected

explanation.correct: In Brazil, the Conditional Script Writer group used by the Scripting Governance Tool can no longer be selected as the assignment group on any task-based record or incident through the UI with the base system configuration. The group exists to grant scripting permissions, so it is kept out of operational assignment. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-identity-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The group still exists in Brazil: the Scripting Governance Tool docs say it grants scripting permissions to its members via the snc_required_script_writer_permission role.
Membership is not tied to admin; auto-assignment adds internal users with one functional role, and the group grants snc_required_script_writer_permission.
Auto-assignment controls who becomes a member of the group; the assignment-group restriction applies in the base system configuration regardless of that setting.

source.excerpt: Prevent the Conditional Script Writer group from being selected as the assignment group on task-based records, so the permission-only group is no longer used for operational assignment target.

questions.question: While planning an upgrade from Zurich to Brazil, an administrator finds that some users still work in the UI15 interface. What do the Next Experience release notes say about UI15?

options.text: It was deprecated in Australia and gets no defect fixes
It was deprecated in Brazil but still receives defect fixes
It stays supported, since just UI11 was deprecated
It was removed from instances during the Australia upgrade

explanation.correct: The Next Experience release notes list one deprecation: starting with the Australia release, the legacy user interfaces commonly referred to as UI11 and UI15 are deprecated. They no longer receive enhancements or defect fixes and will no longer be supported, and the Next Experience is recommended instead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-nextexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The deprecation is listed under Australia, not Brazil (Brazil shows no deprecation updates), and the deprecated UIs no longer receive defect fixes.
Both UI11 and UI15 are deprecated starting with the Australia release.
The Removed section of the Next Experience release notes has no updates for Australia. UI15 is deprecated, and the notes say some system features may still display through legacy rendering paths.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Australia release, the legacy user interfaces commonly referred to as UI11 and UI15 are deprecated.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, an administrator wants to add an application menu with a Dashboard module and a List module without leaving the Next Experience UI to edit UI16 platform records. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Next Experience All Menu Editing from the All menu
UI Builder, creating a separate page for each module
A background script that inserts the module records
The classic UI16 application menu and module forms

explanation.correct: Next Experience All Menu Editing lets admins create and edit application menus and modules directly from the Next Experience UI. It supports Record, List, Dashboard and Custom page modules from a centralized, platform-native interface, so there is no need to navigate to UI16 platform records. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-nextexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI Builder is not needed here; the release notes say menus and modules are created and edited directly from the Next Experience UI with All Menu Editing.
Scripting the records is unnecessary and error-prone; All Menu Editing offers inline configuration of menus and modules with real-time feedback.
The admin wants to avoid UI16 records, and All Menu Editing exists precisely so admins no longer have to navigate to UI16 platform records.

source.excerpt: Create and edit application menus and modules directly from the Next Experience UI. Admins can configure Record, List, Dashboard, and Custom page modules from a centralized, platform-native interface.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, a user's email address was blocked after repeated bounces. The administrator wants to see the original email that bounced. Where can it be viewed?

options.text: The Bounce Email Address Logs list on the address record
The Bounce Email Address Status list in System Mailboxes
The Bounce management component on the Email diagnostics tab
The State field on the Bounce Email Addresses record

explanation.correct: The Brazil Notifications release notes state that the original email associated with a bounced email address can now be viewed from the Bounce Email Address Logs record. Each bounce email address record (System Logs > Bounce Email Addresses) has a Bounce Email Address Logs related list with an Original Email field. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-notifications-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Bounce Email Address Status (System Mailboxes > Administration) is where you configure which status codes are blocked or unblocked by type, class, subject, and detail. It does not hold the original email.
The Bounce management component on the Email diagnostics dashboard shows the total number of hard and soft bounces received within the displayed time frame, not individual original emails.
The State field on a bounce email address record is used to block or unblock the address. The original email is in the Bounce Email Address Logs related list.

source.excerpt: The original email associated with a bounced email address can now be viewed from the Bounce Email Address Logs record.

questions.question: An administrator enables identifier-first login (IFL) on a Service Portal in Brazil. When a user reaches the portal login page, what determines the authentication path they follow?

options.text: The username or email entered, checked against IFL policies
The browser language and time zone reported by the device
The identity provider selected in the portal's login widget
The highest-privilege role currently held by the user

explanation.correct: With IFL in Service Portal, the login page first shows a username/email field. The authentication path is determined by the username or email entered and is evaluated against the IFL policies configured on the instance, and IFL takes precedence over other login options on the portal. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-serviceportal-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The docs say the path depends on the username or email entered and the configured IFL policies; browser language and time zone are not part of it.
IFL takes precedence over any identity provider or local login options configured for the portal, and admins clear those conflicting options when enabling it.
Roles are not what routes the login; the identifier the user types is evaluated against IFL policies to choose the authentication path.

source.excerpt: Use an identifier-first login (IFL) authentication method in Service Portal where the authentication path is determined by the username or email entered, and evaluated against configured IFL policies.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, an administrator wants to share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users without managing individual user, group, or role assignments. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Share it to the dashboard_user role that ships with the base system
Publish its reports so that anyone with the link can view them
Create a group containing every user and then share the dashboard to it
Add each user to the dashboard's sharing list one at a time

explanation.correct: In Brazil, an administrator can share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users by assigning it to the dashboard_user role, which ships with the base system. Any user holding at least one role then gets read access, which replaces managing individual user, group, or role assignments for organization-wide dashboards. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-platformanalyticsexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state it is no longer possible to publish a report; the Read-only link option replaces it and does not share a dashboard organization-wide.
A catch-all group is exactly the kind of group assignment the dashboard_user role approach replaces, and it must be maintained as users join.
Sharing user by user is the individual assignment work the administrator wants to avoid; the dashboard_user role gives every authenticated user read access.

source.excerpt: Administrators can share a Platform Analytics dashboard with all authenticated users by assigning it to the dashboard_user role, which ships with the base system.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, a manager with read-only access to a Platform Analytics dashboard turns on Explore mode to try a different grouping on a visualization. Which two statements describe what happens? (Choose two.)

options.text: The Save action is unavailable while Explore mode is active
The changes last for the current session and are not saved
The changes are saved as a personal copy of the dashboard
The manager must first be granted edit access to it
The changes are shared automatically with the dashboard owner

explanation.correct: The Platform Analytics release notes list Explore mode under Brazil: read-only users can temporarily reconfigure a visualization in-session, on inline dashboards or in the Visualization Designer, without saving changes. When Explore mode is active, an alert says changes aren't persisted and the Save action is not available. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-platformanalyticsexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Explore mode changes aren't persisted. Users reconfigure the visualization in-session without saving changes, so no personal copy is created.
Explore mode lets dashboard consumers explore data on their own terms without requiring edit access.
Explore mode changes are temporary and in-session and aren't persisted, so nothing is shared with the owner.

source.excerpt: Read-only users can temporarily reconfigure a visualization in-session — on inline dashboards or in the Visualization Designer — without saving changes.

questions.question: After an upgrade to Australia, users report that a Core UI report that used to be public is no longer published. Where can a report administrator find it to make it available again?

options.text: The Reports Public [sys_report_public] table
The Analytics Hub page for that public report
The scheduled export library in Platform Analytics
The Publish option in the report's context menu

explanation.correct: The Platform Analytics release notes (Australia changes) state that on upgrade, all public Core UI reports are unpublished to enhance security control. Report administrators can find the unpublished reports on the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table and then make them available through the Sharing UI in the Report Designer. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-platformanalyticsexperience-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: After the Australia upgrade, the Analytics Hub isn't available, and links to it are redirected to KPI Details.
The Brazil notes say Core UI reports are hidden from the scheduled export library page, so it is not where unpublished reports are found.
The release notes say it is no longer possible to publish a report. Publishing was replaced by a Read-only link option in Report Designer.

source.excerpt: On upgrade, all public Core UI reports are unpublished to enhance security control. Report administrators can find the unpublished reports on the Reports Public [sys_report_public] table.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, a service desk lead asks that empty choice-list options show None instead of --None--. Which system property should the administrator set?

options.text: glide.ui.choice.display_none
glide.ui.html.editor.textpatterns
glide.export.xls.max.rows.per.sheet
glide_i18n.ip_geolocation

explanation.correct: The ServiceNow AI Platform core feature release notes list this change under Brazil: configure choice fields to display either None or --None-- for empty options using the glide.ui.choice.display_none system property. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowaiplatformcorefeature-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: glide.ui.html.editor.textpatterns is a Brazil property, but it turns text patterns in the HTML editor on or off. It does not affect choice field labels.
glide.export.xls.max.rows.per.sheet sets the row limit for exports to Excel. It has nothing to do with choice field empty options.
glide_i18n.ip_geolocation is an Australia property that uses a guest user's IP address to set their language. It does not control choice field labels.

documentation.section: ServiceNow AI Platform core feature - Changes

source.excerpt: Configure choice fields to display either None or --None-- for empty options using the glide.ui.choice.display_none system property.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, a user who has only a catalog-related role and no request management role tries to open Request [sc_request] records. What changed in the catalog team's ACL records on that table?

options.text: They no longer give this user access to that table
They still grant access through the catalog admin role
They are left with an empty list of required roles
They now override any other ACL that grants a different role

explanation.correct: The Service Catalog release notes list this under Brazil deprecations: ACL records on request management tables, such as Request [sc_request] and Requested Item [sc_req_item], no longer grant access based on the catalog role or the catalog admin role. Users who have only a catalog-related role and no request management role can no longer use these ACL records to access request management tables or features. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicecatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state that these ACL records no longer grant access based on the catalog role or the catalog admin role.
Each ACL record retains at least one request management role, so the list of required roles is never empty.
The change affects only the ACL records that the catalog team owns. Another ACL record on the same table might still grant access through a different role.

source.excerpt: Users who have only a catalog-related role and no request management role can no longer use these ACL records to access request management tables or features.
